speaker: Doctor
text: That is a very brief start. To begin my assessment of your gait and limb ataxia, could you describe exactly how your walking and coordination have changed over the past few months? Additionally, do you have any specific medical conditions or medications we should review first?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the "drunk" gait and right-sided clumsiness are concerning for cerebellar or spinal pathology. Given your significant medical history, have you ever been diagnosed with syphilis, or are you currently taking any new medications that might cause coordination issues? REQUEST TEST: Serum_RPR_and_TPHA_syphilis_screening.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since syphilis screening is negative, I need to determine if this is a paraneoplastic syndrome or a direct tumor effect. Have you noticed any unintentional weight loss, night sweats, or fatigue recently? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count_and_CRP.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the normal blood work and negative syphilis screen, I need to rule out Vitamin E deficiency, which can mimic this presentation. Have you ever experienced recurrent diarrhea, steatorrhea (fatty stools), or any history of cystic fibrosis or chronic malabsorption? REQUEST TEST: Serum_Vitamin_E_level.

If these results are also normal, I will need to examine your retina and request imaging of your posterior fossa to look for a structural lesion. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Cerebellum_and_Brain_Stem.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Adult Onset Cerebrotendinous Xanthomatosis (CTX)

Based on the negative workup for syphilis, paraneoplastic syndromes, and vitamin deficiency, combined with your ataxia and history, I suspect a metabolic disorder involving lipid metabolism. CTX often presents with cerebellar ataxia in adulthood but is frequently overlooked because the classic cataracts or tendon xanthomas haven't appeared yet. Can you tell me if you have experienced any changes in your vision or notice any yellowish nodules on your Achilles tendons? Also, have you had any family members with similar neurological issues or premature cataracts?
